metadata.title: NAP-001: Plasmid DNA Extraction - QIAGEN QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit
metadata.purpose: Plasmid DNA extraction using the QIAGEN QIAprep Spin Miniprep Kit. Common miniprep kit for cloning, sequencing, ligation, transformation, and screening workflows.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft. Confirm against the current manufacturer protocol, SDS, and local EHS rules before bench use. For this PDF, the miniprep version is selected. Midiprep should become a separate PDF because buffer volumes and columns differ.
beforeYouBegin: Use fresh selective culture. Avoid severely overgrown cultures, mixed colonies, or wrong antibiotic selection.
Check that RNase A has been added to Buffer P1 and ethanol has been added to Buffer PE.
Equilibrate Buffer P1 and N3 if precipitates are present; dissolve any SDS precipitate in Buffer P2 by warming and mixing before use.
For this PDF, the miniprep version is selected. Midiprep should become a separate PDF because buffer volumes and columns differ.

materials.name: Overnight E. coli culture carrying plasmid
QIAGEN Buffer P1 with RNase A
materials.specification: Check that RNase A has been added to Buffer P1

materials.name: QIAGEN Buffer P2
materials.specification: Dissolve any SDS precipitate in Buffer P2 by warming and mixing before use

materials.name: QIAGEN Buffer N3
materials.specification: Equilibrate Buffer P1 and N3 if precipitates are present

materials.name: QIAGEN Buffer PB
materials.specification: Buffer PB if used for optional wash

materials.name: LyseBlue reagent
materials.specification: Optional: LyseBlue reagent if used in the lab to visually monitor lysis and neutralization

materials.name: Purified plasmid DNA
materials.storage: Store plasmid DNA at -20 deg C for long-term storage, or 4 deg C for short-term use if lab policy allows

equipment.name: Microcentrifuge
equipment.settings: Capable of approximately 13,000 rpm / 17,900 x g

tables.title: Run Record Template
rows: Catalog, lot, expiration, and buffer prep notes
tables.note: Blank run-record template provided in the source PDF.

steps.action: Pellet the recommended culture volume by centrifugation. Remove all supernatant so the pellet is not diluted before resuspension.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet completely in 250 uL Buffer P1. Pipette or vortex before lysis until no clumps remain.
steps.criticalNotes: Pipette or vortex before lysis until no clumps remain.

steps.action: Add 250 uL Buffer P2. Mix gently by inverting 4-6 times until the suspension becomes clear and viscous.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not vortex after adding P2.

steps.action: Incubate at room temperature only as allowed by the manufacturer protocol.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not exceed the lysis time limit.

steps.action: Add 350 uL Buffer N3. Immediately invert 4-6 times until the mixture is homogeneous and a white precipitate forms.
steps.expectedResult: The mixture is homogeneous and a white precipitate forms.

steps.action: Centrifuge the lysate for 10 minutes at maximum microcentrifuge speed to pellet cellular debris and chromosomal DNA/protein/SDS precipitate.

parameters.rawText: maximum microcentrifuge speed; approximately 13,000 rpm / 17,900 x g

steps.action: Transfer the cleared supernatant to a QIAprep spin column.
steps.criticalNotes: Avoid disturbing or transferring the white pellet.

steps.action: Optional for endA+ strains or nuclease-rich material: wash the column with 0.5 mL Buffer PB and centrifuge 30-60 seconds.
Wash the column with 0.75 mL Buffer PE and centrifuge 30-60 seconds. Discard flow-through.
Centrifuge the empty column for 1 minute to remove residual ethanol.
Place the column in a clean microcentrifuge tube. Add 50 uL Buffer EB or nuclease-free water to the center of the membrane.

parameters.rawText: 50 uL Buffer EB or nuclease-free water

steps.action: Let stand 1 minute, then centrifuge 1 minute to elute plasmid DNA.

Measure concentration and A260/A280 / A260/A230. Expected plasmid A260/A280 is often near 1.8. Run an analytical gel or diagnostic restriction digest for new clones. Submit for Sanger sequencing across insert/junctions before using the clone as a final validated construct. Store plasmid DNA at -20 deg C for long-term storage, or 4 deg C for short-term use if lab policy allows.

troubleshooting.cause: Low-copy plasmid, poor growth, incomplete resuspension, overloaded column.
troubleshooting.solution: Use fresh colony, correct antibiotic, and kit-valid culture volume; fully resuspend before P2.

troubleshooting.cause: Vortexing after lysis or harsh handling of viscous lysate.
troubleshooting.solution: Invert gently after P2/N3; avoid scraping pellet when transferring supernatant.
Use full PE wash and dry spin; avoid column tip touching flow-through.

troubleshooting.cause: Template too dilute/dirty, primer issue, mixed colony.
troubleshooting.solution: Quantify, re-clean or repeat miniprep from single colony, verify primer.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Use a certified chemical fume hood for phenol, chloroform, TRIzol, guanidinium-containing reagents, and volatile alcohols.
Do not mix guanidinium-containing waste with bleach. Segregate phenol/chloroform/TRIzol waste from aqueous biological waste according to institutional EHS instructions.
Use nuclease-free tubes and filtered tips. For RNA work, use RNase-free consumables and decontaminate work surfaces before starting.
Confirm ethanol has been added to wash-buffer concentrates when required. Mark bottle labels with date, initials, and ethanol volume added.
Record sample input, reagent lot, elution/resuspension volume, concentration, purity ratios, storage location, and deviations.
